# Voyager 1 and Voyager 2 major heliospheric boundary crossings.
#
# Sources:
#   Termination shock V1: Stone et al. (2005), Science 309:2017-2020,
#     doi:10.1126/science.1117684
#   Termination shock V2: Stone et al. (2008), Nature 454:71-74,
#     doi:10.1038/nature07022
#   Heliopause V1: Gurnett et al. (2013), Science 341:1489-1492,
#     doi:10.1126/science.1241681; Burlaga et al. (2013), Science 341:147-150
#     doi:10.1126/science.1235451
#   Heliopause V2: Burlaga et al. (2019), Nature Astronomy 3:1007-1012,
#     doi:10.1038/s41550-019-0920-y; Stone et al. (2019), Nature Astronomy 3:1013-1018
#     doi:10.1038/s41550-019-0928-3
#
# Format: spacecraft  boundary           crossing_date       approx_distance_AU  notes
#
# All crossing times are given to day precision. Sub-day precision is
# available in the cited papers but not required for CD associator evaluation.
#
# Crossing definitions:
#   termination_shock: inbound crossing where solar wind speed dropped to zero
#     and plasma pressure increased sharply (V1 and V2 each had multiple nearby
#     crossings over several days; the date given is the first confirmed crossing).
#   heliopause: final crossing into the Very Local Interstellar Medium (VLISM)
#     where suprathermal electron oscillations and magnetic field direction
#     changed abruptly.
#
spacecraft  boundary             crossing_date         distance_AU  reference
V1          termination_shock    2004-12-16            94.0         Stone2005
V2          termination_shock    2007-08-30            83.7         Stone2008
V1          heliopause           2012-08-25           121.7         Gurnett2013
V2          heliopause           2018-11-05           119.0         Burlaga2019
